KB14.title: Clean Cotton Picking and Moisture Standards
KB14.content: Pick seed cotton only when bolls are fully opened and dried after morning dew evaporates (after 9:30 AM). Keep stained, insect-damaged bolls (kawadi cotton) separate from clean first-quality cotton. Do not use plastic/fertilizer polypropylene bags for picking; use clean cotton cloth bags to prevent polypropylene fiber contamination.
KB14.citation: Central Institute for Research on Cotton Technology (CIRCOT) 2025

KB14.title: Paddy Harvesting Moisture and Combine Operation
KB14.content: Harvest paddy when 80-85% grains in panicles turn straw golden yellow and grain moisture is between 20-22%. Delayed harvesting causes grain shattering and sun cracking, leading to high broken rice percentage during milling.

KB15.title: Grain Drying and Safe Storage Moisture Levels
KB15.content: Dry harvested paddy down to 14% moisture content for short-term commercial storage and 12-13% for long-term seed storage. Use Hermetic PICS (Purdue Improved Crop Storage) bags or metallic silos to prevent rice weevil (Sitophilus oryzae) and Angoumois grain moth infestation without chemicals.

KB15.title: Chilli Sun-Drying, Aflatoxin Prevention and Cold Storage
KB15.content: Dry harvested red ripe chillies on clean polythene sheets or cement drying floors (kalams), never on bare soil. Moisture must be reduced to 10% or below to inhibit Aspergillus flavus growth and aflatoxin contamination. Cold storage at 4-6°C with 65-70% relative humidity preserves bright red color and capsaicin content for up to 10 months.
KB15.citation: Spices Board of India Post-Harvest Quality Manual 2025
